input: Investigate co-ownership mortgage schemes for first buyers

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Co-ownership covers several distinct schemes (shared ownership, shared equity, guarantor mortgages, joint borrower sole proprietor, etc.) — knowing which to include or exclude shapes the entire research scope.

Schemes, eligibility rules, and lenders vary significantly by country and region (e.g. England, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland each have different government-backed products), so location is critical.
Co-ownership implies more than one party — knowing who the co-owner(s) would be (partner, friend, family member, housing association) changes which schemes are relevant and how they work legally.
Deposit size, income level, and credit situation directly determine which schemes the user actually qualifies for, making budget and financial position a key filter.
Whether the user wants a summary document, a comparison table, links to official sources, or advice on next steps (e.g. speaking to a broker) determines the format and depth of the output.
The user may want to simply understand the landscape, shortlist schemes to apply for, or make a final decision — the end goal defines how thorough and actionable the research needs to be.
The user may prioritise minimising monthly payments, maximising the share they own, avoiding government ties, or other values — this steers which schemes to emphasise in the findings.

gold.taskTitle: Investigate co-ownership mortgage schemes for first buyers
gold.taskDescription: Research available co-ownership mortgage schemes suited to first-time buyers to inform a potential property purchase decision.

questions.title: Which specific co-ownership schemes should be included?
questions.description: Clarify whether to cover all co-ownership types (shared ownership, shared equity, joint borrower sole proprietor, guarantor mortgages, etc.) or only particular ones the user has in mind.

questions.title: Which country or region will the purchase be in?
questions.description: Identify the target location (e.g. England, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, or elsewhere) to ensure only locally available and legally relevant schemes are researched.

questions.title: Who would the co-owner be in this arrangement?
questions.description: Establish the relationship of the co-owner (romantic partner, friend, sibling, parent, housing association) as this determines which scheme types are legally and practically applicable.

questions.title: What deposit amount and income level are you working with?
questions.description: Understand the user's rough financial position — deposit saved and combined income — to filter research to schemes they actually qualify for.

questions.title: What format should the research output take?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a written summary, a comparison table, a list of official links, or a step-by-step action plan to speak with a broker or apply.

questions.title: What decision will this research help you make?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is general awareness of the landscape, shortlisting schemes to pursue, or having enough information to take immediate action with a lender.

questions.title: What matters most to you in a co-ownership arrangement?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priority — e.g. lowest monthly cost, owning the largest possible share, flexibility to buy out the co-owner later, or avoiding government scheme conditions.
